ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the figure below, place M is seasonally affected by the prevailing westerlies, place N is affected by the prevailing westerlies year-round, and the west sides of both M and N are ocean. Read the figure and answer: <image1> What is the prevailing near-surface wind direction at place M?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two rectangular regions on the left and right; the left figure marks point M, and the right figure marks point N; both figures have a latitude line marked 40°, and point M is located near the 40° latitude line in the left figure and above that latitude line. The stem also states that the west sides of both M and N are ocean, and that place M is seasonally affected by the prevailing westerlies. Then reason: Place M belongs to the seasonal westerly-controlled area near 30°—40° on the west coast of a continent; in the figure M is located on the equator side of the 40° line, corresponding to north of 40°S in the Southern Hemisphere. The near-surface airflow of the Southern Hemisphere prevailing westerly belt generally goes from west to east, and is deflected to the left by the geostrophic deflection force, so the direction from which the wind comes is the northwest direction. Therefore the prevailing near-surface wind direction at place M is northwest wind.
